reading.title: One Word, Two Meanings
reading.purpose: Hear more words that mean two different things.
paras: Some words have two meanings. A watch tells time, and you watch a show. A train rolls on tracks, and you train for a race. A stick comes from a tree, and glue makes paper stick.
A pencil has a point, and a game has a point. You duck low, and a duck swims. Mean words are unkind, and a red light means stop. Be kind and fair at the fair.

qs.q: A game has a point. What is a point in a game?
qs.why: In a game, a point is a score. On a pencil, it is the sharp end.

qs.q: Which word can name a bird that swims?
qs.why: The reading says a duck swims.

qs.q: Be kind and fair at the fair. What is the fair?
choices: A place with games and rides.
qs.why: The last fair names a place. The first fair means treating everyone the same.

needsReview.reason: Dense word-play; a teacher may want to read it slowly with pictures. The last sentence plays on fair/fair.
